This file is the contract. BYTE-IDENTICAL TWIN:
Each repo asserts its OWN implementation reproduces `expected_props` for the given `wire`
item, so a change on one side turns the other repo's suite red. Update BOTH copies together.
Comparison normalization (applied identically on both sides):
1. null / undefined values are dropped recursively (Ruby emits nulls, JS omits keys);
2. `articles[i].id` is replaced with `"__RELATED_ID_<i>__"` (the Ruby side reads real
autoincrement ids, the wire carries fixed ones — everything else is compared verbatim).

cases.name: unicode separators — U+2028 heading, BOM heading, BOM in the summary
_why: Ruby and JS disagree on two string questions, and each disagreement was invisible on
first load (Ruby, always right) and wrong on SPA navigation:
1. Ruby '.' excludes only \n, JS '.' also excludes U+2028/U+2029 - so an H2 carrying a
LINE SEPARATOR matched HEADING_LINE in Ruby and did not match in TS, and the whole
TOC entry vanished after a click-through.
2. Ruby [[:space:]] and JS /\s/u differ on exactly U+0085 (Ruby only) and U+FEFF (JS
only) - so a BOM inside a heading slugified to 'byte-order-mark' in TS and
'byteorder-mark' in Ruby (a dead anchor), and a BOM inside the summary made TS think
the summary restated the title and drop the standfirst the server had rendered.
Codepoints are written as \u escapes so this file stays ASCII and the separators cannot
